articles.description:
Originally published on Medium.
Most AI agent demos put the model on top of the database. The agent gets a "query" tool, the user asks a question, the model writes the query. It works great in a demo. In production, it means the model's judgment is the only thing standing between a user and someone else's data.
I'm building an AI agent into The Arsenal, a platform for life insurance agents. The first version is boring on purpose: it reads performance data, answers questions, and writes nothing. But even a read-only agent sits on top of client records, so I'm working through the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications item by item before the agent exists. This post is item two, sensitive information disclosure, and the design decisions that came out of it.
The model never touches the database. It…
articles.title: My AI Agent Never Touches the Database

articles.description:
AI assistants are starting to call businesses' systems on behalf of their users: "return the blue jacket", "move my appointment to Thursday". Reading an order is harmless. A refund moves money, and that's where the interesting engineering is.
Here are the four failure modes I'd design for first, with the TypeScript I use for each. The examples use allowfy, a small open-source package (zero dependencies, Web Request/Response), but the patterns apply to any webhook-based integration.
Your refund endpoint will be reachable from the internet. Every request must prove it came from your gateway, and be recent.
The scheme: Allowfy-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">. Verify over the raw body, before any JSON parsing, with a constant-time comparison and a time wind…
articles.title: Handling AI agent refunds without paying twice: signatures, idempotency and limits in TypeScript

articles.author: Tim Apple
articles.description:
Two of the terminal tools now have proper homes on the web: fm-cli.ninepointlabs.com and autonomix-cli.ninepointlabs.com. Until today, the only way to learn about either one was its GitHub README.
Each site is one page that answers the questions you’d have before installing: what the tool does, how to install it on your system, and how to get started. Both link straight to the latest release, and the full command reference stays in the README for when you need it.
fm-cli is Fastmail from the terminal: a full-screen mail app, commands that print JSON, and a live watch that follows your mailbox over Fastmail’s push connection. The site walks through all of it, including offline mode, the two-week calendar agenda and contacts, and how sign-in keeps tokens in your system keyring. It also shows every way to install it:
# On Omarchy
omarchy-mise-install github:ninepointlabs/fm-cli fm-cli

# With mise anywhere else
mise use -g github:ninepointlabs/fm-cli@latest

There are .pkg.tar.zst, .deb and .rpm packages and plain tarballs for Linux and macOS too. The README’s screenshot was also swapped for one showing sample mail.
Autonomix CLI installs and updates apps straight from GitHub Releases. The site covers the package formats it understands, how it detects what’s already installed, the JSON output for scripts, and how it fits into Omarchy: the bar widget and the post-update hook that updates your apps whenever you run omarchy update. Install steps for Debian and Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch are right there, along with the full command list.
A website is easier to share and easier to read than a repository. If you’ve been sending someone a GitHub link to explain what fm-cli or Autonomix CLI is, you can send them the site now. Nothing changes in the tools themselves, so there’s nothing to update.
Originally posted on blog.ninepointlabs.com.
articles.title: fm-cli and Autonomix CLI get their own websites

articles.description:
Short answer: make failure recovery produce a verified disposition, not a better-sounding guess. For a healthcare appointment assistant, keep source identity and revision time attached to every passage, retry only idempotent reads inside a fixed deadline, and switch to a clarifying question or handoff when evidence is empty, stale, or contradictory.
I treat retrieval as an evidence pipeline with a stop condition. The language model is the last consumer of that pipeline, not its repair mechanism. A patient asking for the earliest cardiology slot next Tuesday needs a grounded statement about availability and clinic policy; a fluent answer assembled from an old index is an operational incident wearing a friendly tone.
No guesswork.
Before choosing a replica, define the states the assistant ma…
articles.title: Grounded Recovery Playbooks for Healthcare Appointment Assistant Retrieval Under Load

articles.author: Papan Sarkar
articles.description:
A codebase I got through Fiverr looked like an ordinary Next.js invoice app. It wasn't.
Two dependencies deep, gated behind an npm auth token committed in the project's own .npmrc, sat a private package carrying roughly 180 KB of heavily obfuscated JavaScript — wired to execute every time the dev server starts.
I caught it before running it. Here is the short version.
package.json scripts held only dev, build, start and lint. No preinstall, no postinstall, no prepare.
A grep for the usual suspects came back empty:
grep -rnE "eval\(|new Function|child_process|execSync|spawn\(|atob\(|fromCharCode|base64" \
  --include=*.js --include=*.mjs --include=*.cjs --include=*.ts --include=*.jsx --include=*.tsx . \
  | grep -v node_modules

A long-line grep, which is how whitespace-padded payloads usua…
articles.title: How a Clean Next.js Repo Ran Malware on Every npm run dev

articles.description:
I have a number of old and new virtual machines, and need to ssh from each VM to the host.
Therefore install an ssh server:
# apt install openssh-server

And configure it to allow incoming connections from older VMs:
/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/allow-older-clients.conf
# When a client ssh fails to login, look at the "service sshd status" log,
# and by use of "man sshd_config" find the options that need additional values.
Ciphers +aes128-cbc,aes192-cbc,aes256-cbc
KexAlgorithms +diffie-hellman-group1-sha1,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1
HostKeyAlgorithms +ssh-rsa
